title: Assemble the Brief, Exceptions and All
scenario: It is 6:50 AM on the messy morning. The brief must ship with everything this day actually was: a delegated approval, a dropped row, a missing forecast, an unknown generation status. An honest brief does not hide its exceptions - it gives them a section. Fill every slot from your stored artifacts.
input: Assembly rule: every slot value comes from a stored artifact - look it up, never re-derive. Template v1.1.0 includes the new Data Notes section (per the template change), which reports today's exceptions: the hub whose feed row was dropped and the hub excluded from variance. The approval line must show the delegation. The headline hub is the one risk-evaluation.json marks escalate.
instructions: Open each artifact on the shelf as you need it.
Fill the approval line from the delegated approval record - including why a delegate decided.
Fill the headline from the risk record and prices from the clean table.
Fill Data Notes: which hub's row was dropped, which hub had no forecast.

## Headline
{{headlineHub}} moved {{headlineMovePct}} percent day-over-day (peak {{peakPrice}}, settled {{settledPrice}}).

## Hub Summary
ERCOT peak 204, settled 151. SPP peak 98.5, settled 90. WAUE peak 63, settled 58.

## Operations
Generation status not reported this morning (intake recorded null).
## Data Notes
{{droppedHub}} row dropped at cleaning (missing settled value). {{missingForecastHub}} excluded from variance (no forecast for this hub yet).
Prepared by the Meridian workflow at 6:50 AM.

copilotPrompt: Assemble a brief from stored artifacts: delegated approval facts (status, deputy, time, reason) from the approval record, the escalated hub and move from the risk record, its prices from the clean table, and the two Data Notes exceptions - the hub dropped at cleaning and the hub excluded from variance.
successMessage: Brief rendered with its exceptions on the page. Honest output beats tidy output.

intro.heading: Before you assemble: the brief tells the whole truth

sections.title: Exceptions are content, not noise
sections.body: This morning dropped a row, skipped a comparison, and delegated an approval. Readers acting on this brief NEED those facts - a brief that hides its gaps invites decisions the data cannot support.

sections.title: Two slots you derive by ABSENCE
sections.body: The dropped hub is the one in the raw feed but not the clean table; the missing-forecast hub is classified in risk but absent from variance. Reading what is NOT in an artifact is a real assembly skill - lineage reasoning, not lookup.

sections.title: The template you changed, in use
sections.body: Data Notes exists because of the change request you assessed in the template lesson - approved by the owner, versioned to 1.1.0, present every day. Today it has content; on quiet days it will say none.

takeaway.heading: Honest brief assembled
points: You shipped a deliverable that reports its own gaps - the dropped row and the missing forecast are on the page, not buried in logs.
The approval line shows the delegation and why, straight from the substitution record.
Two slots came from lineage reasoning (what is absent between artifacts), not simple lookup - assembly at this tier reads the pipeline, not just the files.
Every exception in Data Notes traces back to a governed decision you made earlier this morning.
The workflow can now produce an output that is trustworthy BECAUSE it is honest about what it does not know.
